article.headline: The Retroactive Oracle: Fintwit's Favourite Boast Genre
article.lede: A recurring ritual on financial social media: the poster who, once prices have moved, excavates a forgotten call and presents it as prophecy. The "no one cared" gambit flatters the poster's foresight while quietly burying the question of how many other calls went unacknowledged for good reason.
article.body:
The post follows a template as old as stock-market braggadocio itself: a list of tickers, entry prices, and percentage gains, accompanied by a lament that the wisdom was ignored at the time. What goes unexamined is the denominator — the calls that did not appear on the victory-lap list, the positions that quietly expired unannounced. Survivorship bias is the silent co-author of every such thread, and "no one cared" is its most polished marketing copy.

The basket itself, however, reflects some genuine 2025-2026 market narratives rather than random picks. The largest reported winner, Ondas Holdings ($ONDS), is a drone and autonomous-systems company whose stock surged on defence contracts, a border-security order, and a pending merger with Bethesda-based prime contractor Mistral — a firm with over a billion dollars in Department of Defense indefinite-delivery contracts. The drone-to-defence-prime story is verifiable and substantial, even if the 1,600% figure strains the credibility of a planned purchase at $0.71.

Also real: the *bitcoin-miner-to-AI-HPC pivot* trade, a structural theme in which companies originally built to run power-hungry mining rigs discovered that the same scarce megawatts, retooled for *high-performance computing* (HPC) — GPU clusters for artificial-intelligence workloads — could generate far more durable revenue from hyperscaler tenants. IREN Limited (formerly Iris Energy) signed a $9.7 billion, five-year cloud-computing deal with Microsoft. Cipher Mining rebranded as Cipher Digital and secured a fifteen-year, 300-megawatt lease with Amazon Web Services estimated at $5.5 billion. TeraWulf moved from bitcoin to contracted AI-infrastructure revenue, with hyperscaler deals anchoring a $900 million equity raise in April 2026. These are not rumours; the contracts are on file with the SEC.

The remaining names are more heterogeneous. AST SpaceMobile ($ASTS) is building a *direct-to-device* satellite broadband network — satellites that communicate with ordinary smartphones, no special hardware required — backed by carrier agreements with AT&T, Verizon, and Vodafone. The stock ran to an all-time high of roughly $130 in January 2026 on commercial launches and revenue that grew 641% year-over-year, then retreated sharply. D-Wave Quantum ($QBTS) hit $46.75 in October 2025 on a wave of *quantum computing* enthusiasm partly triggered by Nvidia's Ising-model release, before losing more than half that peak value. Opendoor ($OPEN) became a 2025 meme stock in the original sense — retail energy detached from fundamentals — after co-founders returned, injected $40 million of their own capital, and rebranded the distressed *iBuyer* (a company that buys homes algorithmically for resale) as an AI platform. Revenue fell roughly 34% year-over-year in Q3 2025; the stock's trajectory owed more to Shopify's ex-COO taking the helm and Reddit enthusiasm than to any improvement in the housing market.

What is not verifiable, and should not be taken on faith, is that any specific entry price was actually traded at the claimed level on the claimed date. The post provides no screenshot of a brokerage confirmation, no dated archive of the original call, no accounting of position size. A person who bought $100 of ONDS at $0.71 and sold at $7.50 made $956; a person who bought $10,000 and rode it to $12 then watched it halve made something quite different. The genre thrives on omitting all three of those variables. The stocks are real, the sector rotations are real, and some of the returns — properly sized and timed — would have been remarkable. Whether @sunxliao was actually aboard for any of them is a matter of faith the market cannot settle.
article.fact_check: The retroactive-entry-price post is a well-established genre on financial social media whose defining feature is the absence of contemporaneous evidence. The specific tickers listed do correspond to real companies that experienced large 2025-2026 price moves: Ondas Holdings rallied sharply on defence-drone contracts; IREN, Cipher Digital, and TeraWulf are genuine bitcoin-miner-to-AI-HPC pivot stories with publicly filed contracts with Microsoft and AWS; AST SpaceMobile reported 641% revenue growth on its satellite broadband build-out; D-Wave Quantum surged and retreated on quantum-computing sentiment; and Opendoor was widely documented as a 2025 meme-stock rally driven by retail and co-founder re-entry. No brokerage confirmation, dated archive post, or position-size disclosure accompanies the original claim, making the entry prices unverifiable. NUAI could not be confidently identified as an active publicly traded US company and was excluded from ticker modules.

ticker_asts.name: AST SpaceMobile, Inc.
ticker_asts.blurb: AST SpaceMobile is building a network of large-aperture satellites in low Earth orbit designed to deliver broadband directly to unmodified standard mobile handsets — no specialised hardware required. The company has carrier partnerships representing roughly three billion potential subscribers, including AT&T, Verizon, Vodafone, and Rakuten, and secured $1 billion in hard commercial commitments from those partners.
ticker_asts.recent: BlueBird 6, described as the largest commercial communications array ever deployed in LEO, launched aboard an ISRO LVM3 rocket in December 2025. The company targets intermittent US nationwide service in early 2026 and continuous service by late 2026, with 45-60 satellites on orbit by year-end. A 10-year commercial agreement with stc Group (Saudi Arabia) was signed in October 2025.

sources.title: BlueBird 6 launch announcement (BusinessWire)

AST stc Group 10-year deal (SatNews)

ticker_cifr.name: Cipher Digital Inc. (formerly Cipher Mining Inc.)
ticker_cifr.blurb: Cipher Digital (originally Cipher Mining) began as an industrial-scale bitcoin miner and pivoted aggressively toward AI and high-performance computing infrastructure. The company rebranded in February 2026 to reflect its strategic transformation away from cryptocurrency toward hyperscaler data-centre hosting, leveraging its power-dense facilities and existing infrastructure relationships.
ticker_cifr.recent: Cipher secured a 15-year, 300-megawatt lease with Amazon Web Services estimated at approximately $5.5 billion in contract value, and a 10-year, 300-megawatt lease with Fluidstack and Google. The company now holds 600 megawatts of contracted HPC capacity. Q1 2026 bitcoin mining revenue was $34.8 million while the company absorbed a wider net loss of $114.3 million as it funds the HPC build-out. Stock rose roughly 300% over the trailing twelve months through mid-2025 before the HPC pivot announcement triggered a near-term sell-off on dilution concerns.

sources.title: Cipher Digital rebrands and pivots from bitcoin mining to HPC (CoinDesk)
CIFR stock AI hyperscale deal news (StockTwits)
Bitcoin miners going all-in on AI, selling BTC (CoinDesk)

ticker_iren.name: IREN Limited
ticker_iren.blurb: IREN Limited (formerly Iris Energy) is an Australian-founded, NASDAQ-listed company that began as a renewable-energy-powered bitcoin miner and has since pivoted aggressively toward AI and high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructure. The company controls significant power capacity — a scarce resource in the AI data-centre boom — across sites in North America, and rebranded from Iris Energy to IREN in November 2024 to signal the strategic shift.
ticker_iren.recent: IREN reported its first profitable fiscal year in 2025, with net income of $86.9 million on $501 million in revenue. A $9.7 billion, five-year cloud-computing agreement with Microsoft was signed in late 2025, calling for deployment of 76,000 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs across 200 megawatts at its Childress, Texas campus. The company targets scaling GPU capacity from 23,000 to 140,000 units through 2026, backed by 2,910 megawatts of renewable power infrastructure.

sources.title: IREN bitcoin-to-AI pivot deep dive (FinancialContent)

ticker_onds.name: Ondas Holdings, Inc.
ticker_onds.blurb: Ondas Holdings is an autonomous systems and drone technology company operating through two main segments: Ondas Autonomous Systems (drone and counter-drone platforms) and Ondas Networks (industrial wireless communications). Its Iron Drone Raider counter-UAS system and Optimus autonomous drone platforms serve defence, homeland security, and industrial customers in the US, Europe, Israel, and the UAE.
ticker_onds.recent: Ondas delivered 605% revenue growth in 2025, with Q4 2025 revenue of $30.1 million — up 629% year-over-year. A pending $175 million merger with Mistral, a Bethesda, MD-based prime contractor with over $1 billion in existing DoD IDIQ (indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity) contracts, was announced. The company secured US border-security drone contracts. Stock rallied over 1,000% from 52-week lows, driven by defence-drone demand and the Mistral deal, before analysts cautioned on execution risk at elevated multiples.

Ondas border-drone contract and 700% rally (ts2.tech)

ticker_open.name: Opendoor Technologies, Inc.
ticker_open.blurb: Opendoor is an iBuyer — a company that purchases homes algorithmically for rapid resale, aiming to bring liquidity and simplicity to the residential real-estate transaction. It went public via SPAC in 2020 at elevated valuations, then suffered a protracted decline as rising interest rates crushed housing-market transaction volumes and compressed the margins on its home-flipping model.
ticker_open.recent: In mid-2025, Opendoor became a retail-driven meme stock, rising roughly 237% from July lows as co-founders Keith Rabois (who became chairman) and Eric Wu rejoined the board, injecting approximately $40 million of personal capital. Kaz Nejatian, formerly COO of Shopify, was named CEO in September 2025 and described a pivot to an AI- and software-driven platform under the 'Opendoor 2.0' framing. Q3 2025 revenue fell 34% year-over-year with a net loss of $90 million. The stock subsequently retreated sharply after earnings disappointed and the meme-momentum dissipated.

sources.title: Opendoor meme rally and AI pivot analysis (247wallst.com)

ticker_qbts.name: D-Wave Quantum Inc.
ticker_qbts.blurb: D-Wave Quantum is a Canadian-founded quantum computing company that commercialises quantum annealing — a technique suited to combinatorial optimisation problems — and, after its January 2026 acquisition of Quantum Circuits Inc. (QCI) for $550 million, also operates gate-model quantum hardware. It is one of the few publicly traded pure-play quantum computing companies.
ticker_qbts.recent: QBTS reached an all-time high of $46.75 in October 2025 partly on a sentiment surge following Nvidia's release of Ising quantum AI models, before retreating to roughly $21 by May 2026. Full-year 2025 revenue was $24.6 million (up 179% year-over-year) but the company reported losses of $355 million. D-Wave closed the year with $884.5 million in cash, providing runway despite deep unprofitability. Analyst views are sharply split: median price targets imply substantial upside while some analysts cite extreme overvaluation versus near-term fundamentals.

sources.title: D-Wave Quantum extreme valuation vs execution (Seeking Alpha)
QBTS stock price and 2026 outlook (blockchainreporter.net)
D-Wave Quantum stock forecast and price target 2026 (MarketBeat)

ticker_wulf.name: TeraWulf Inc.
ticker_wulf.blurb: TeraWulf is a power-infrastructure company that began as a renewable-energy-powered bitcoin miner and has pivoted toward high-performance computing (HPC) and AI data-centre hosting. It operates the Lake Mariner facility in New York and the Nautilus Cryptomine joint venture in Pennsylvania, with a focus on nuclear- and hydro-powered compute capacity — a differentiator in an era of AI-driven power scarcity.
ticker_wulf.recent: By early 2026, more than 50% of TeraWulf's revenue derived from HPC hosting, up from approximately zero two years prior, anchored by multi-year contracts with Core42 and Fluidstack. In April 2026, the company raised over $900 million in a common-stock offering to fund Lake Mariner HPC build-out phase 3 and retire convertible debt. The stock moved from a 52-week low near $3.18 to a high of roughly $19.31, a gain of approximately 507% over the trailing twelve months, though at a price-to-book ratio far above industry norms.

poster_sunxliao.notes: Posts in the 'retroactive call' genre common on financial social media: lists of tickers with claimed entry prices and subsequent gains, framed as ignored wisdom. No confirmed institutional affiliation or track record documentation found at time of writing. Posts skew toward volatile, narrative-driven names across sectors including bitcoin miners pivoting to AI, drone/defence, meme stocks, and speculative technology.
